title: Your YouCoded plan, in one place

steps.path: The first screen of your private planning Page
steps.headline: What should the planning Page help you understand first?
steps.today: YouCoded's direction, roadmap entries and detailed plans live in separate documents. Their current status still needs checking, and the Page has not been designed.
steps.problem: When you open a shared plan, it may be hard to tell the long-term vision from the work that needs attention now.
steps.proposal: Choose what the opening view puts first. The Page can still link the vision, active work and detailed plans; this is about what you see first.

options.label: Vision first
pros: Shows what the work is ultimately for.
Makes it easier to see how individual plans fit together.
cons: You may need to look further down to find what needs attention now.

options.label: Active work
pros: Puts current priorities and ongoing work within easy reach.
Helps you decide what to look at next.
cons: The long-term direction may feel less prominent at first.

options.label: Balanced overview
pros: Shows direction and current work together.
Avoids making either one the whole story.
cons: Each part may get less room and detail on the opening view.

steps.path: Editing an initiative or opening its detailed plan
steps.headline: What should you be able to edit directly on the planning Page?
steps.today: Planning is kept in version-controlled records and linked Markdown plans. The private Page is not built yet; public information is intended to be a separate, read-only snapshot.
steps.problem: If every change means leaving the Page to edit files, small planning updates can feel cumbersome. Editing long documents in a compact view may also get in the way.
steps.proposal: Choose how much editing belongs on the Page. Detailed plans can remain openable as documents either way.

options.label: Planning fields
options.summary: Edit the structured planning details on the Page; open detailed plans as documents to edit them.
pros: Makes common updates quick and easy to scan.
Keeps long-form writing in the document where it is easiest to work.
cons: You leave the Page to revise a detailed plan.

options.label: Edit plan documents
options.summary: Also edit the full linked plans directly in the Page.
pros: Lets you read and revise a plan without switching views.
Keeps more of the planning work in one place.
cons: Long documents can be harder to edit comfortably in a planning view.
The Page has more editing controls to learn.

steps.page: Choosing which files Pages can use
steps.intro: These questions are about reusable file access for Pages—not a general file browser.

steps.path: Choosing files or a folder for a Page to use
steps.headline: How should you let a Page keep access to your files?
steps.today: Pages can keep their own small data and make mediated network requests, but they do not have general access to your device's files.
steps.problem: A Page that works with your documents would otherwise need you to choose files again and again—or might ask for broader access than you intended.
steps.proposal: Choose how ongoing access should work. Access would be limited to what you approve, shown when the Page asks, and revocable; reading and changing files would be separate permissions.

options.label: Choose files each time
pros: You decide exactly which files are available for each task.
Nothing keeps access to a folder in the background.
cons: Repeated work means choosing the same files again.

options.label: Grant a folder
pros: A Page can keep working with files in a folder you chose.
You do not have to pick the same files every time.
cons: You need to review and revoke folder access when you no longer want it.

options.label: Both choices
options.summary: Choose individual files for one-off work, or grant a folder for ongoing work; manage and revoke folder access later.
pros: Fits quick tasks and repeated work.
You can choose a smaller set of files when that is all a Page needs.
cons: There are two ways to choose access, so the choice needs a clear explanation.

steps.path: Reviewing what will appear on the public planning page
steps.headline: How should you approve updates to the public planning page?
steps.today: The public view is intended to be a generated, read-only snapshot. Private planning content must be left out, not sent to a public page and merely hidden.
steps.problem: A private note or unfinished plan appearing publicly could reveal information you never meant to share.
steps.proposal: Choose when a public snapshot may be updated. Its contents should be shown for review before publication, with private material excluded from the public output.

options.label: Approve each update
pros: You see the proposed public information before it goes live.
Nothing new is published until you approve it.
cons: You must review and approve every update.

options.label: Approve content changes
pros: You review changes to what the public can see.
Routine updates that do not change public content need not interrupt you.
cons: You need a clear way to tell content changes from routine updates.

options.label: Keep it private
pros: No planning information is published publicly.
You can revisit public sharing later.
cons: Visitors cannot see an up-to-date public planning page.
